assertion_analysis.tests/test_fleet_health_records_node_tmp: Fails if any of the four independently literal disk names disappears or changes relative order; does not compare the production schema to itself.
Fails if source moves after the first disk field; canonical schema extensions after disk fields remain permitted.
Fails if production queries a scheduler executable other than squeue through the injected runner.
Fails if the production scheduler call omits or changes its ten-second timeout.
Fails if the terminal observation does not stop after one scheduler call; an extra call changes the observed calls list.
Fails if append overwrites any existing prefix bytes; the prefix is a pre-call persisted snapshot, so this is a preservation check rather than a disk-measurement claim.

Fails if append changes the pre-existing header; columns was used to create the initial file, not passed into the function under test, so the before/after comparison protects preservation and is not credited as independent schema correctness.
Fails if the scheduler row is dropped, appended twice or the node row is lost.
Fails if the retained node row source is changed from its literal node marker.
Fails if append changes the original node memory reading from its literal 37.
Fails if the appended row does not identify the scheduler source.
Fails if the recorded terminal state differs from the independent scheduler response CANCELLED; this checks serialization, not discovery of a real scheduler state.
Fails if a terminal CANCELLED scheduler response is classified or persisted as anything other than end; this is the derived event needed to stop the reader.
Fails for the nonempty extra-columns parameter if scheduler rows invent metric values rather than the literal dash; the empty parameter alone is vacuous and is not credited for this guard.
Fails if an appended row has excess fields, which DictReader reports under a None key; it is not credited as detection of too few values.
Fails if removing any one of the seven required fields no longer raises FleetNodeError with the named refusal; removing the guard or omitting a required name would make its parameter case fail.
Fails if refusing the malformed header alters any file bytes; before is a persisted pre-call snapshot, a valid nonmutation assertion.
